Code-switching by Portuguese-German bilinguals

Source: R/data.R
code_switching.Rd

Switches between Portuguese and German in conversations of 90 speakers of Portuguese heritage in Germany, 30 from each of three generations. Each speaker is recorded in four conversations on different topics, with a bilingual or a monolingual (German) interlocutor. Second-generation speakers switch most, and more of their switches fall within a sentence. Speakers rarely switch with monolingual interlocutors. For count models with an exposure.

Usage

code_switching

Format

A tibble with 360 rows and 8 columns:

speaker

Speaker ID, S01 to S90.

generation

"first", "second" or "third".

conversation

Conversation ID (speaker_topic).

topic

"family", "work", "leisure" or "migration".

interlocutor

"monolingual" or "bilingual".

utterances

Utterances by the speaker in the conversation.

switches

Switches between the languages.

intrasentential

Of these, switches within a sentence.

Source

data-raw/code_switching.R

Details

True model: switches are negative binomial (size 6) with mean rate * utterances, where rate is 0.04 (first), 0.12 (second) or 0.07 (third generation), multiplied by 1.3 (family), 0.8 (work), 1 (leisure) or 1.1 (migration), by 0.25 with a monolingual interlocutor, and by a speaker effect (SD 0.35 on the log scale). Intrasentential switches are binomial with probability 0.25, 0.6 and 0.4 for the three generations.

References

Poplack, S. (1980). Sometimes I'll start a sentence in Spanish y termino en español: Toward a typology of code-switching. Linguistics, 18(7-8), 581-618. doi:10.1515/ling.1980.18.7-8.581

Examples

head(code_switching)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 8
#>   speaker generation conversation  topic     interlocutor utterances switches
#>   <fct>   <fct>      <fct>         <fct>     <fct>             <int>    <int>
#> 1 S01     first      S01_family    family    bilingual           114        6
#> 2 S01     first      S01_leisure   leisure   bilingual           144        2
#> 3 S01     first      S01_migration migration monolingual         125        0
#> 4 S01     first      S01_work      work      bilingual            91        8
#> 5 S02     first      S02_family    family    bilingual           183        8
#> 6 S02     first      S02_leisure   leisure   bilingual           145        5
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: intrasentential <int>
